summary: Feed s156_double to IDS is degraded: 14.8% frames sliced to ~192 bytes and 10.4% TCP packets show missing data/sequence gaps. IDS requires full payload and both directions - slicing blinds payload inspection and breaks TCP reassembly.

findings.root_cause: Packet broker has slicing/snaplen enabled at ~192 bytes, cutting frames short before delivery. Evidence shows 456 of 3077 frames (14.8%) truncated, most to 192 bytes.
findings.impact_on_tool: IDS needs_full_payload=true for signature and anomaly detection. Truncated payload hides application data, exploits and C2, causing missed detections and evasion.

recommended_fix.why: IDS requires full payload up to 1518 bytes. Disable slicing / set snaplen >=1518 for this IDS feed to deliver complete frames.

findings.root_cause: Same slicing configuration is causing apparent packet loss: broker forwards sliced frames so TCP sequence analysis by IP length shows gaps. 310 of 2985 TCP packets (10.4%) show missing data, well above 1% threshold. Feed is confirmed sliced.
findings.impact_on_tool: IDS TCP reassembly and stream tracking fails with missing segments. Results in incomplete flows, missed alerts, and degraded detection coverage for multi-packet attacks.

recommended_fix.why: Removing slicing restores full packet length and eliminates sequence gaps. If slicing is needed for other tools, create an unsliced replica or increase snaplen to max_frame_bytes 1518 for this IDS feed.
